agree.reason: A quick reader gets a clear case: he runs a milking shift on his own, has a strong attendance record, caught mastitis cases early using data, and is already working on his English, so a doubtful committee member would probably move toward yes.

honest.reason: The letter adds things the brief doesn't support: 'Nobody asked him to learn it', 'he came back and picked up right where he left off', 'he does it right' and 'seriously ill'; it also leaves out that he gave only two days' notice before leaving.

works_the_facts.reason: The attendance figure is left as 'two shifts in three years' when it could be shown in its strongest form: about 780 scheduled shifts with 2 missed, or more than 99.7% attendance; the mastitis count is also never tied to the size of the herd.

right_comparison.reason: Calling him 'one of the most dependable people on my staff' is the only comparison, and it gives no basis such as how often others miss shifts or who else could cover the 3 a.m. shift, so the committee can't tell how he stands against other applicants.

qualification.reason: This is a recommendation without reservations, and the one weakness (written English) is stated openly, so no conditional hedge is needed.

objections.reason: The letter deals directly with the likely concerns about his written English and the five-week absence and turns both to his credit, though it avoids the short notice he gave rather than addressing it.

fit.reason: It is a one-page reference letter from the farm manager with the right opening, a contact offer and a signature block, which is what the brief asked for.
